title: First Doctor Visit
subject: Health
setting:
A doctor's office. You are the patient visiting with general illness symptoms — a headache, tiredness, fever, and cough.

---
goal: Say you feel sick and name basic symptoms
Answer a doctor's simple questions
Understand basic medical instructions (rest, medicine, come back)

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Hello. What is your problem?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Hello. I feel sick.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: What do you feel?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I have a headache and I feel tired.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have a fever?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, a little.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: How long do you feel like this?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Two days.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have a cough?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, I cough a little.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Okay. I will check you now.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: You have a mild infection. You need rest and water.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: I will give you medicine. Take it two times a day.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Come back if you feel worse.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I understand. Thank you, doctor.

title: Body Parts and Symptoms
subject: Health
setting:
A doctor's office. Two different patients each describe pain across several body parts and receive advice.

---
goal: Name body parts when describing pain or discomfort
Describe multiple symptoms at once
Understand a doctor's recommendations including nurse and hospital

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Hello. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Hello doctor. I feel sick.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: What do you feel?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I have pain in my head and a headache.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have a fever?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, and I have a cough and a cold.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you feel pain in your throat or chest?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, my throat hurts and my chest hurts.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: What about your stomach or back?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: My stomach hurts a little, and my back hurts too.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do your arms or legs hurt?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: My arm hurts, but my leg is okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: I will check your eyes and ears.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: You need medicine. You can get it at the hospital.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Thank you, doctor.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Hello. What is the problem today?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Hello doctor. I feel bad.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Where do you have pain?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I have pain in my hand and my leg.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have a fever or a cough?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: No fever, but I have a small cough and a cold.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do your eyes or ears hurt?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: My eye hurts, but my ear is okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have a headache or toothache?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, I have a toothache.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: How is your throat and chest?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: My throat is okay, but my chest hurts a little.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: I will ask the nurse to help.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: You need medicine and rest. If you feel worse, go to the hospital.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Thank you, doctor.

title: Explaining How It Started
subject: Health
setting:
A doctor's office. Two patients each explain symptoms connected to something they did — a walk and a day of heavy work.

---
goal: Tell a short story that explains how symptoms began (I went for a walk, I carried heavy things)
Describe where pain moves in the body
Use natural phrases like "I think" and "a little"

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Hello. What brings you in today?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Hello doctor. I went for a walk, and later I feel pain in my stomach.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: I see. Is the pain sharp, or more like pressure?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I don't know the word… it just hurts here, in the stomach.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: That's okay. Does the pain move to your back or chest?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, a little to my back. Chest is a little pain too.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you also have a fever, cough, or cold?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: No fever. Small cough.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Any headache or toothache?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: No toothache. Small headache before.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: How about your throat, does it hurt when you swallow?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Throat is a little pain, yes.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: I'll check your eyes and ears, and then your stomach.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Your symptoms are mild. I think you need rest and some medicine.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay, thank you doctor.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: If the pain gets worse, go to the hospital or come back.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I understand. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Hi. Can you tell me what's been bothering you?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Hello doctor. Yesterday I work, and my arm and hand start to hurt.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: What kind of work were you doing?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: I carry heavy things. After that, pain in arm and hand.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Understood. Does the pain go down to your leg or stay in the arm?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Only arm and hand. Leg is okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have any fever, or signs of a cold or cough?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: No fever. No cold. Small cough before, but now okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Any pain in your chest or back?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Back a little pain. Chest no.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do your eyes or ears feel normal?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Yes, eye and ear okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: And no headache or toothache?

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: No, only arm pain.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Alright. I think this is from the strain. The nurse will help you with some medicine.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Rest your arm and hand. If it gets worse, you should visit the hospital.

lines.speaker: Patient
lines.text: Thank you doctor.

title: Opening an Account and Withdrawing
subject: Bank
setting:
A bank branch. A customer visits to open a new account and deposit cash. A second customer comes in to withdraw money and asks about a future transfer and loan.

---
goal: Open a new bank account using a passport
Deposit cash and ask about your balance
Withdraw money and get a receipt

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Hello. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hello. I want open bank account.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Of course. Do you already have a passport with you?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes, I have passport here.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Great. I'll also need your signature on this paper.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay. Here?

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Yes, right there. Would you like a card for the account as well?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes please. I need card for ATM and payment.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: No problem. Do you want to deposit any money today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes. I want deposit cash.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Alright. I'll put the money into your new account.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you. Can I see balance now?

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Yes, I'll print a receipt with your balance on it.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay, thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Hi. What can I do for you today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hello. I need take money from account.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: You'd like to withdraw money?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes, withdraw money.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: No problem. Do you have your card or passport?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I have card.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Thank you. How much cash would you like?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Two hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Alright. Your balance is still good after this withdraw.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay. Also, I want transfer money next week.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: That's fine. We can help you with the transfer when you come back.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay. And maybe loan later.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Sure, we can also talk about a loan in the future.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: You're welcome. Here's your cash and your receipt.

title: Transfers, Loans, and Currency Exchange
subject: Bank
setting:
A bank branch. A customer handles several transactions in one visit — withdrawing cash, making a transfer, asking about a loan, depositing a check, and exchanging currency.

---
goal: Withdraw a specific amount and request banknote sizes
Sign paperwork and make a transfer to another account
Ask about a loan, deposit a check, and exchange currency

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Hello. What can I help you with today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hello. I want withdraw money from my account.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Of course. How much would you like to withdraw?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Three hundred dollars. Also, can you tell me my balance?

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Yes. Your balance after the withdraw will be one thousand dollars.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay, good. I also want transfer money to another account.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: No problem. Please write the account number here and add your signature at the bottom.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay. Done.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Thank you. Do you want the money as large banknotes or small banknotes?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Small banknotes please.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Alright. Here is your cash and your receipt.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Hi. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hello. I want ask about loan for car.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Sure. Do you already have a savings account with us?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes, I have savings account here.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Great. We'll need your signature on these papers.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay. Also, I forget my PIN for my card.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: That's alright. We can help you change it today.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Good. And I have one check to put in account.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: You'd like to deposit the check?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes, deposit check.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: No problem. Do you also need currency exchange today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes, I want exchange shekels to dollars.

lines.speaker: Bank Worker
lines.text: Alright. Here is your receipt for the deposit and exchange.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you very much.

title: Getting to Your Destination
subject: Taxi
setting:
A taxi ride to a hotel near the airport. The passenger boards, gives the destination, and at the end pays with cash and receives change.

---
goal: Tell a taxi driver where you are going and give an address
Choose between route options (fast vs. cheaper)
Pay for the ride and handle change

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Hello. Where are you going today?

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Hello. I go to hotel.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Sure. What's the address?

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: One moment… here. This street.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Alright, I know it. It's near the airport.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Yes, correct.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Do you want the fast way or the cheaper way? There's a lot of traffic right now.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Fast please.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: No problem. Please put your bag in the back.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: If you need anything, just tell me.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Okay, thank you driver.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: We're almost there. Your hotel is on the right.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Should I stop here or closer to the door?

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Closer please.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Alright.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: This street very busy.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Yes, traffic is always slow here in the evening.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: How much for ride?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: It's twenty dollars.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Okay. I pay cash.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: Thank you. Let me get your change.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.text: You're welcome. Have a good evening.

lines.speaker: Passenger
lines.text: You too.

title: A Very Long Day
subject: Review
setting:
A casual conversation with a friend. You explain your very busy day — starting with waking up with pain, going to the hospital by taxi, and then continuing to the bank for several transactions.

---
goal: Tell a story in past tense connecting multiple locations and events
Describe a full day at the hospital, in a taxi, and at the bank
Practice all vocabulary from Lessons 1–6 in one natural conversation

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Hey! How was your day today?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Very busy day. I wake up early because I have pain in my stomach and back.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Really? Was it bad pain?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Not very bad, but enough to go hospital and see doctor.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: How did you get there?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I take taxi to hospital.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Was the traffic bad?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, very slow. The driver say traffic near airport always slow in morning.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you know the hospital address?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I had address on my phone. I show driver the street.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Nice. So what did the doctor say?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Doctor ask many questions. He ask if I have fever, cough, cold, headache.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Small headache and little cough, but no fever.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did he check you?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes. He check my stomach, back, throat, chest, eyes, and ears.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Sounds serious.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: No, doctor say it is okay. Maybe stress and bad food.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did he give medicine?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, medicine and rest.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Good. Then what happened?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: After hospital I take another taxi to bank.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Again traffic?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, but this driver go fast.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: What did you need at the bank?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Many things. First I withdraw cash.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Three hundred dollars. Then I check my balance.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Was your balance okay?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, okay. Not amazing, but okay.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you talk to the bank worker in English?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, but sometimes difficult.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: What was difficult?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Words like transfer and receipt.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Ah yes, those are hard at first. Did you make a transfer too?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, small transfer to another account.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you need your signature?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes. I write signature many times.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you use your card?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, and I also use ATM outside bank.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Any problem with your PIN?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: No, this time okay. Last month I forget PIN.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you ask about a loan too?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, small loan maybe next year.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Sounds like you did everything today.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, hospital, taxi rides, bank… very long day.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: At least your English gets better.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Slowly better, yes. Talking helps a lot.

title: Hardware Store: Shopping for Supplies
subject: Hardware Store
setting:
A hardware store. A customer needs tools and supplies for a home painting project — hammer, nails, paint, brush, tape, and a ladder. They then pay at the cashier.

---
goal: Ask a store worker where to find specific tools and supplies
Explain what you need the items for
Pay at the cashier with a card and handle the receipt

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: Hello. Can I help you find something?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Hello. Yes, I need tool for home.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: Sure. What kind of tool are you looking for?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I need hammer and nails. Also screws.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: No problem. The screws and nails are on the left. The hammers are next to the drills.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay. I also need paint.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: What color paint do you want?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: White paint for small room.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: Alright. Do you already have a brush?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: No, I need brush and tape too.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: Painter's tape?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes, tape for paint.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: Great. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Maybe ladder. Small ladder.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: Those are near the back wall.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Okay thank you. My English not very good.

lines.speaker: Worker
lines.text: You're doing fine.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Hi. Did you find everything you needed?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes, I think so.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Alright. I see paint, a brush, screws, nails, tape, and a battery.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes. Battery for drill.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Got it. Are you paying cash or card today?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Card please.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Okay. You can enter your PIN here.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: One moment… okay.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Perfect. Do you want the receipt?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes please.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Here you go.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Are you working on something at home?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes. Small problem in room. Need paint and tool.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Makes sense. Hopefully the ladder helps too.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes. Last time I stand on chair. Bad idea.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Yeah, a ladder is much safer.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Yes. Also my back still has pain from last time.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Ouch. Be careful this time.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: I will. Thank you.

title: Building a Shelf at Home
subject: Hardware Store
setting:
At home, building a shelf and painting a room with a friend. The tools were bought at the hardware store the day before. The conversation moves naturally between the work and stories from previous days.

---
goal: Use tool names and action words while doing practical work
Give and follow step-by-step instructions during a task
Hold a casual conversation while doing physical work (connecting back to previous lessons)

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Hey! Sorry I'm late. The traffic was very slow today.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: No problem. Come in.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Wow, this room already looks different. Almost like a hotel room now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Thank you. But still much work to do.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: So what do we need to fix first?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: First, shelf on wall. Then paint. Then clean everything.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Sounds good. Did you buy all the tools?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I go hardware store yesterday.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Nice. What did you get?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Hammer, screws, nails, drill, tape, brush… many things.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Good. Do you also have pliers and a wrench?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, here in this box.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Perfect. Where's the wood for the shelf?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Here, next to ladder.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Alright. I think we should build the shelf first before we paint.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, good idea.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Can you carry that wood for me?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes… wow, heavy. My back still has little pain from last week.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: From the hospital visit?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. Doctor say rest, but I do room work anyway.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: That sounds like a bad idea.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Maybe. But room need fixing.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Fair enough. Hand me the drill.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Here.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: And the screws too.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Hmm… this wall is stronger than I thought.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Need bigger drill?

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: No, this one is okay.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I also buy extra battery for drill.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Smart. Last time my battery died in the middle of work.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I remember. We finish very late that day.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Alright, now hold the shelf here.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Like this?

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Little more left. Yes, perfect.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Good?

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Yep. Now I'll fix it to the wall.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Okay, shelf is done.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Wow, looks good!

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Now we can paint. Where's the paint and brush?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: On the floor near the tape.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you buy glue too?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. Maybe for small problem near window.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Good idea.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I think white paint is better for room. More light.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Definitely. The room already feels bigger.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Can you help me move this box?

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Sure. What's inside?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Old tools, bank papers, receipts… many things.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Haha, you keep everything.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. Even old bank receipt from when I withdraw cash.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: That's very organized actually.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Okay, ready to paint?

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Ready. But first, let's clean the wall a little.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Good idea.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Hey, pass me the saw.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: This wood is too long for the shelf. I need to cut it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Ah okay. Here.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Thanks.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: You know many tools.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: My father taught me when I was young.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I still learn English and tools at same time.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Honestly, you're doing well with both.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Slowly better. Practice helps.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Exactly. By the end of today, you'll know every word in the hardware store.

title: Breakfast with Wife and a Waiter
subject: Restaurant
setting:
A café in the morning. You sit down with your wife for breakfast. She asks about the previous day — finishing the room, going to the bank, and a taxi problem. A waiter then takes your order.

---
goal: Describe yesterday's activities to a family member
Order food and drinks using polite restaurant language
Handle a small mistake with the order gracefully

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Good morning. You look tired today.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I still have little cough and my throat hurts a bit.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Is it from the cold you had last week?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I think so. But now much better than before.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Did you finally finish the room yesterday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Almost. I still need to fix one shelf because the plank is too long.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Did you carry the wood upstairs again by yourself?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. Bad idea. My back hurts now.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: You really need help sometimes.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I know. But after we paint the wall, the room looks much nicer.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: That's true. Did you also go to the bank yesterday?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. I needed to make deposit and check my savings balance.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Was everything okay there?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Almost. I forgot my signature on one paper.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Again?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. The bank worker looked very tired of me.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Did you also ask about the loan?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: A little. But I think maybe next year.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: And how did you get there? Taxi again?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. The traffic was terrible near my old address.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Morning traffic is always horrible there.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, and the driver gave me wrong change after I paid.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Did you notice immediately?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: No, only later when I checked the receipt.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Ah, that's annoying.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, but not big problem. Oh look, waiter is coming.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Good morning! Here are your menus. Are you ready to order?

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: I think so.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Can I ask something first?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Of course. What would you like to know?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Which sandwich do you recommend?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: The chicken sandwich is very popular, and the soup today is also excellent.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Does the soup come with salad?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Yes, a small salad on the side.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Okay. I want sandwich.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Great. And for drinks?

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: I'd like a decaf cappuccino with soy milk please.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Absolutely.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: And for me, long double espresso please. No sugar.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Certainly. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: One chocolate cake to share.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Perfect. I'll place the order now.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: My pleasure.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Your English is getting more natural now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Sometimes yes, but long explanations are still difficult.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: But today you explained many things very well.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I try. Words like deposit and exchange are still hard for me.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: You used them correctly though.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, but I need more practice.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: That's normal. I still remember when you only knew "bank" and "money."

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: True. Now I can explain traffic problems, wrong address, receipts… many things.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Exactly. And you can even explain home repairs now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. I know plank, shelf, wood, paint… too many words now.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Soon you'll work in hardware store.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: No thank you. Too much carrying heavy wood.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Here you are — one chicken sandwich, one soup and salad, one decaf cappuccino with soy milk, one long double espresso, and one chocolate cake.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Sorry, I think the cake is missing.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Oh, you're absolutely right. I'm sorry about that. I'll bring it immediately.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: No problem, thank you.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: And here's the cake. Enjoy everything!

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Thank you!

title: Street & City: Driving Through the City (Part 1)
subject: Street & City
setting:
Driving a friend through the city after a day of work together. The friend is the passenger pointing out landmarks and helping with directions.

---
goal: Describe what you see while driving — buildings, traffic, pedestrians
Give and receive driving directions
React naturally when you miss a turn

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Thanks again for helping me with the room today.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: No problem. The shelf is much better now.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Yes, the paint also looks good.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, the room looks clean now.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: My cough is finally better.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Good. My cold is also almost gone.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: This street is always busy.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, a lot of traffic here.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Look at that building.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I see it. I never noticed it before.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: There is a traffic light.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I see it. It is red. I will stop.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: That bus is very big.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, many people inside.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: A bicycle is coming.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I will wait.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Look at the pedestrian.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: He is crossing the street.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: You need to turn here.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Oh… I missed the turn.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Again?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I was not paying attention.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Do you know the address?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I have it on my phone.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: That store looks new.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I did not see it before.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: This park is small.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, but nice.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: There is a bridge behind it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I see it now.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: You are not very good with directions.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: True. I focus too much on traffic.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: You still have my exchange receipt?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I think it is in my bag.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Good. And your signature was correct at the bank?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, this time I checked it twice.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Good job.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I am trying to remember everything better.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Now just drive slowly.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I will stop at the next sign.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Then I will get out at the corner.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Okay, I will stop there.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Thanks for the ride.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: No problem. See you next time.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: And try not to miss the turn next time.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I will try…

title: Street & City: Driving Through the City (Part 2)
subject: Street & City
setting:
Continuing a car ride to drop a friend off at their home, a few minutes after the previous driving conversation. The two reflect on the day's work and notice things along the route.

---
goal: Observe and comment on city scenes during a car ride
Connect the day's activities to past lessons naturally
Navigate to a destination while having a real conversation

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: We still have a few minutes before we get to my house.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, the traffic is moving slowly today.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Look at that truck in front of us.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, it is very big. I would not want to drive that.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Me neither. I prefer a normal car.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Same. Parking must be difficult with a truck.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: There are a lot of trees on this street.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I like that. It makes the street look nicer.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Oh, look at that dog.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, it is running very fast.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: The owner is trying to keep up with it.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: The dog looks like it has a lot of energy.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: That park is busier than before.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I can see more people there now.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: See that bench near the crosswalk?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. Two people are sitting there.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Sometimes I sit there when I wait for a taxi.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Really? I usually just stand and wait.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Look at the fence around that building.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Maybe they are fixing something there.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Could be. The building looks old.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, maybe they are painting it.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: That reminds me, are you happy with the paint we used today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I think the color looks much better than before.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: I agree. The room feels bigger now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: And much cleaner too.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Did you remember to put all the tools away?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, everything is back in the box.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Good. Last time we spent twenty minutes looking for the hammer.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, and it was on the shelf the whole time.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: We are almost at my address now.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, just one more turn.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: The traffic light is green. Good timing.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Finally. We waited a long time at the last one.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: I think that store sells bicycles.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, I can see several bicycles in the window.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Maybe I should buy one.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Then you won't need a taxi so often.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: True. It would also be cheaper.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: And probably faster when there is a lot of traffic.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Okay, this is my corner.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Great, I will stop here.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Thanks again for helping with the room and for the ride.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: No problem. It was a good day.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: See you next week.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: See you!

title: A Day at the Gym
subject: Gym
setting:
A gym visit with your wife. First at the front desk to renew the membership, then a water break mid-workout to catch up with each other.

---
goal: Handle a simple membership transaction at a gym reception desk
Describe a workout using body vocabulary and past and future tense
Practice invisible grammatical particles — ש, את, ל, כי, כש, and ה-agreement — in natural conversation

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Welcome to the gym! Can I help you?

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Yes. We'd like to renew our membership.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Of course. What name is it under?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I think it's under my name — Mark.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: I can see that you have a family membership.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, that's right. For both of us.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: It expires at the end of the month. How many months would you like?

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Three months, please. Is the price the same as before?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes, 350 shekels per person. Shall I renew the membership now?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes please. I'll pay with a card.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Do you also need a locker today?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. Do you have a free locker?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The free locker is number eight. Here is the key.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Is that the locker that's near the changing rooms?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes, exactly.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Perfect. Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Let's take a break. My legs are already tired.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Me too. I think I trained too hard today.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Did you remember to bring a towel and a bottle?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, they're in my locker.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: You lifted very heavy weights. Did you do a proper warm-up?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes, but my back hurts because the exercises were too heavy for me.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: I think you should rest for a few minutes.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. I also have pain in my arms.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: I ran on the treadmill for twenty minutes. Now I want to do some stretches.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Good idea. Actually, let me ask that man first about the machine.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Excuse me, how many sets do you still have on this machine?

lines.speaker: Gym-goer
lines.text: Just one more.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Thanks. I'll wait here.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Can you put the heavy weights back when you're done?

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Of course. But the trainer told me I should carry less next time.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: You look strong today, though.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I don't feel strong. I think I have a muscle strain.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: When you have a strain, you should stop immediately.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: I know. When I finish this exercise, I'll stop.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: Don't forget — we're going to the ice rink tonight. Your ice skates are in the car.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Yes. I hope I can still skate — my legs are already so tired.

lines.speaker: Wife
lines.text: The training session was too long today. Next time we should rest more between exercises.

lines.speaker: Me
lines.text: Agreed. Let's go get changed.

title: The Physio Session
subject: Health
setting:
Mark drops in to see the physiotherapist at his office — she already knows him and his shoulder history. He explains the inflammation has come back and is causing neck tension and headaches. She examines him, treats him, and sends him home with exercises and a follow-up appointment.

---
goal: Describe a recurring health issue and explain how one symptom leads to another
Understand and follow a physiotherapist's instructions during treatment
Use function words — at least, actually, at all, anyway, in other words, still, just, specifically, even — naturally in conversation

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Hey Mark, sit down. What's going on today?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: My shoulder is hurting again. I think the inflammation is back.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: When did it start this time?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: About a week ago. At first it was just the shoulder, but now my neck hurts too.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: And headaches?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes. I even have headaches now. I can't even turn my head properly.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's what usually happens with your shoulder. The inflammation causes bad posture, and the posture causes tension in the neck.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: In other words, the shoulder is causing all of it. Actually, I think the gym made it worse this week.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's possible. Hold your arm out to the side for me.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Like this?

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Yes. Do you feel pain when I press here?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, specifically there. Not at all on the other side.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: And when you sit at a desk for a long time, does it hurt there too?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, specifically then. It just starts hurting, for no reason.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's the posture. When you sit badly, the back muscles tighten.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: My back hurts too, actually. I forgot to mention that.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Let me check your back as well. Does the tension spread to your throat?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, when the headache is really bad, my throat feels tight too.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: I'll work on the muscle now. Breathe in and then release.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Now breathe normally and try to release the shoulder completely.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I can't even do that. The muscle won't let go.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's okay. Is there tightness in the chest as well?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just when I breathe deeply.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: All connected. At least the neck is not too bad yet.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: At least. Still, the headaches are really bothering me.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: The headaches will improve once the shoulder improves. Let me press a bit deeper. Try to breathe through it.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. Anyway, I should have come to the physiotherapist earlier this week.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's what I always say. Don't wait until it gets this bad.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. I don't always notice when it gets worse.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Do you even do the exercises I gave you at all?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Honestly, not every day.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's why it keeps coming back. The exercises are what keep the inflammation from getting worse.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. I'll do better.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: I'm busy tomorrow, but come in on Thursday for another treatment.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thursday works. Is my company coverage still valid for more sessions?

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Yes, you still have four sessions left. Plenty.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good. At least I don't need to worry about that too.

title: Back at the Physio
subject: Health
setting:
Mark comes in for a follow-up session a few days after the last visit. His shoulder has improved since he started doing the exercises, but now the neck and headaches are the main problem. The physiotherapist focuses on the neck this time, talks through his posture at work, and sends him off with neck exercises he can do at his desk.

---
goal: Report a health update — what improved and what's still a problem — and explain how symptoms connect
Understand and follow a physiotherapist's instructions during treatment
Use function words — at least, actually, at all, anyway, in other words, even, exactly — naturally in conversation

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Come in, Mark. How's the shoulder since last time?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Better, actually. The inflammation is almost gone. But my neck is really bothering me now.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: And headaches?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, every day. The pain just won't let go in the mornings.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Did you do the exercises?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Most days. I skipped a couple of days at the gym, but otherwise yes.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Good — that's probably why the shoulder improved. Sit down and let me check the neck.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Okay. It hurts most right here.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: I can feel the tension. When I press here, does the pain go up to your head?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, exactly there. That's where the headache starts.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's the neck muscle — it's too tight. It won't let go on its own.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I thought it would improve a bit on its own. At least a little.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: The shoulder, yes. But the neck — not at all. Lie down and breathe normally.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Like this?

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Yes. I'll press on the neck now. Tell me if it hurts too much.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: It's strong, but okay. I can feel it releasing a bit.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Good. Try to breathe and not hold your chest.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sorry. I always do that when something hurts.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: How's your posture at work? Are you sitting properly?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: No, not properly. I sit at a desk for hours and don't even notice.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: That's causing a lot of this. The neck tension comes from the back.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: In other words, even when the shoulder is fine, the posture is still the problem.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: You need to fix how you sit, not just treat the pain.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Exactly. I know. It just happens — I don't notice it at all.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Any pain in the arm or the chest?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just a bit in the arm when I lift it. No chest pain at all, actually.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: I'll do a few more minutes on the neck, then I'll check the back.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Anyway, I should have come in earlier this week. I waited too long.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: When the headaches start, come in. Don't wait until it gets worse.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Exactly — I just didn't think that it would hurt this bad.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: You have two sessions left on your insurance. Come in next week.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Is Tuesday okay?

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Yes. And let me show you the neck exercises — you can do them at your desk.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'll do them properly this time.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Good. The exercises are what keep the inflammation from coming back.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: In other words, I need to do them every day, not just when it hurts.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Move your head slowly to the side and hold for ten seconds.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Like this?

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Yes. Twice a day, both sides.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: At least they're easy. That's something.

lines.speaker: Physio
lines.text: Good. See you Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Anyway, thank you. See you then.

comments.author: Nadav
comments.text: פחות תפוס — alternative for "I can feel it releasing a bit" (lit. "less tense/tight")

comments.author: Mark
comments.text: replaced with "that it would hurt this bad" in the lesson

comments.author: Mark
comments.text: Commented this before: just use simple words like "move" not "tilt" unless it's in the word list.

title: At Ben Gurion Airport
subject: Travel
setting: Ben Gurion Airport, departure hall. Mark is traveling alone to Amsterdam for his sister's wedding. He has one suitcase and a backpack. He moves through three checkpoints in sequence: a short security interview before the check-in queues, the check-in counter where he drops his suitcase, and the bag screening belt before the gates. Three conversations, one right after the other.
goal: Navigate all three airport checkpoints — security interview, check-in, and bag screening — without losing the thread
Use airport vocabulary — suitcase, boarding pass, gate, scanner — without hesitating
Connect explanations naturally with because, so, and when — in the security interview and at the check-in counter

verbs: To board / get on the plane

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: Passport, please. Where are you flying today?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: To Amsterdam. Here you go.

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: What is the purpose of your trip?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: My sister is getting married in Amsterdam.

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: How long will you be there?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: About a week. I'm flying back next Sunday.

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: Did you pack your suitcase yourself?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, I packed it myself. I'm traveling alone.

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: Is anyone carrying something for you, or did someone ask you to carry something for them?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: No, nothing.

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: Where will you be staying?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: At my parents' house, not a hotel this time.

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: Is your passport still valid?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, it's valid for another four years.

lines.speaker: Security Officer
lines.text: Good. You can go to check-in. Have a good flight.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: Good morning. Passport and reservation, please.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Here's my passport. I have a booking on the afternoon flight.

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: Are you checking a suitcase?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, one suitcase and a backpack.

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: Your suitcase weighs 26 kilos. That's over the limit. You'll need to pay for extra baggage.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: That's fine. Where do I sign?

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: Sign here, please. Window or aisle seat?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'm very tall. Is there a seat with more legroom?

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: I can put you in the front row. Aisle seat?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Perfect, that works great.

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: Here is your boarding pass. Gate 22, Terminal 3.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you. Is the flight full today?

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: Very crowded, yes. Boarding starts in two hours.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: One more thing. Is there a currency exchange in the terminal?

lines.speaker: Check-in Agent
lines.text: Yes, just after security, on the left. Have a good flight.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Security Screener
lines.text: Next in line, please. Put your bags on the conveyor belt.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Of course. One moment.

lines.speaker: Security Screener
lines.text: Take off your belt and put it in the tray.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: OK.

lines.speaker: Security Screener
lines.text: Do you have a laptop? Take it out of the bag.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, here it is.

lines.speaker: Security Screener
lines.text: Do you have any liquids?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: No, I left them at home.

lines.speaker: Security Screener
lines.text: Step through the scanner, please.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: Security Screener
lines.text: Please wait. Do you have anything in your pockets?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sorry, I forgot my phone.

lines.speaker: Security Screener
lines.text: Take it out and go through again. Then you can collect your things.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Of course. Thank you.

comments.author: Mark
comments.text: This sentence is really hard to directly translate to hebrew.

comments.author: Mark
comments.text: Reservation does not exist in this context, they would ask for tickets.

title: At the Supermarket
subject: Shopping
setting: After the gym, Mark and Heli stop at the Carrefour below. They need yoghurt and milk. A quick loop through the store to find what they need, then straight to the checkout for the usual round of questions.
goal: Handle the standard Israeli checkout questions — club card, points, donation, split payment — without stopping to think
Ask a staff member for directions inside the store and understand location-based answers (aisle, section, in front, turn)
Use supermarket vocabulary — yoghurt, cart, sale, expiry, fresh — naturally in a familiar scene

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: It's really crowded today. Let's be quick.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I know. We just need yoghurt and milk.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Excuse me, can you help me find the yoghurt?

lines.speaker: Staff Member
lines.text: Yes. Continue to the end of this aisle and turn right. It's in the dairy section, right in front of the milk.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you, I'll find it.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Here it is. All the dairy products are right here.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: There are so many kinds. I never know which one to take.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Look, the Greek yoghurt is on sale this week.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good. Let me check the price and the expiry date.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: This one is fresh. Take it.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Can you recommend a flavor? I always just take the natural one. I don't even check.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Take the vanilla one. It's really good.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: OK. Is it still fresh? Can I exchange it if it's not?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Yes, just keep the receipt. The checkout is open, let's go.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Got it. I'll take the cart.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Good evening. Do you have a club card?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, here you go.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: I'll scan it. You'll collect points on this.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good. How many points do I have so far?

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: I can't see that here, check in the app. One-shekel donation to charity?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, I'd like to donate.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Would you like to pay in one payment or split it?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: One payment, please. We're paying by card.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: That's 54 shekels. Sign here, please.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Of course. And we don't need a bag, we have a backpack.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: One moment, the machine is a bit slow.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: No problem, we can wait.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Did we remember to check if we need coffee?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I think we still have some. We'll check when we get home.

lines.speaker: Cashier
lines.text: Great. Here's your receipt. Have a good evening.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Thank you, you too.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thanks. Have a good one.

title: A Kerach Evening
subject: Social / Sport
goal: Handle a full social evening in Hebrew — greeting friends, catching up on the ice, making plans as a group, and ordering at a restaurant
Use future tense and time expressions naturally when making and discussing plans
Reinforce sport, social, and food vocabulary from previous lessons in an easy, familiar setting
setting: A Tuesday evening at the ice — the rink where Mark and Heli go every week with their group of friends. Most of the group is already there when they arrive: Aref, Noya, Dea, and others. After an hour of skating and catching up, Dea suggests Agadir for dinner, and the evening ends with the whole group at one big table.

lines.speaker: Aref
lines.text: Finally! We've been here for twenty minutes already. How are you?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Good, sorry. The traffic from the gym was terrible tonight.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Aref, is the ice full already?

lines.speaker: Aref
lines.text: Very full. The whole group is here, and there are a lot of kids too.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Wait, did you remember the wrist guards?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, they're in the bag. Yours and mine.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Are your laces okay? Give me your hand and I'll hold the skate.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: They're a complete mess again. I can never get them right.

lines.speaker: Aref
lines.text: Are you doing a quick stretch first, or going straight on?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'll stretch here and then go. The ice looks really slippery tonight.

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Come on, I want to start. What are you still doing?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: One second. I still need to put on my knee pads.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: Let's finally catch up properly. It's been two weeks. How was the Netherlands?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Really nice. My sister's wedding was beautiful. But I'm still tired from the trip.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: Look at Heli over there. She's already out there skating. She's really something.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: She waits for this all week. That spin she just did, she's been practising it for months.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: Try to stop here. Push your heels out to the sides like this.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I always forget how to do it. On slippery ice it's so much harder.

lines.speaker: Noya
lines.text: Mark! When did you get here? I didn't even see you come in!

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just now. Noya, how are you? What's going on with the army?

lines.speaker: Noya
lines.text: The army is fine. But don't even ask about my boyfriend right now. It's a whole story.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Are you okay? Do you want to talk about it later?

lines.speaker: Noya
lines.text: I'm fine, don't worry. Oh, watch — Mishel almost just crashed into that kid over there.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I saw that. I was sure they were both going to fall.

lines.speaker: Dea
lines.text: Okay, everyone, who's up for going out tonight? I suggest Agadir.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'm in. I've been thinking about the Agadir burger for the last hour.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: Did everyone agree on Agadir? I heard there might be a wait tonight.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I think so. Let's try to leave in twenty minutes. Did Dea already make a reservation?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Come on, let's go take off our skates.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I'll come with you. I want to take off my knee pads too.

lines.speaker: Michael
lines.text: Wait, I need to stop at the ATM first. I have no cash on me.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Me too. Is there one near the exit?

lines.speaker: Dea
lines.text: I called Agadir and made a reservation for ten. It's going to be a great evening.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Perfect. Let's go. Everyone's ready.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Good evening! Are you all together?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yes, we reserved a table for ten. The name is Heli.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: I have you right here. Come this way. Can I start with some water for the table?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Yes please. And can we see the menus?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you. And some bread while we wait, if you have it.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Of course. Tonight's special is the Angus burger with Agadir fries.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: That's exactly what I wanted. Can I get it with cheddar?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: No problem. And for you?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: I'll have the Caesar salad, please.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Great. Anything else to start?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: I think we're good. Actually, can we also get more water for the other end of the table?

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Here we go. Everything's out. Enjoy!

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: Thank you, it looks amazing.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Thank you so much. Exactly what I needed after a long evening.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.text: Whenever you're ready, the bill is here. All together or separately?

lines.speaker: Heli
lines.text: All together. Should we go to the cashier or can we pay here?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Just bring us the card machine. We'll pay here.
